❯ Without using any tools, explain in about 40 lines how a hash map works. Use a heading, two short paragraphs, a
  bulleted list of 6 items, a numbered list of 4 steps, a small table, and a short Rust code block.

⏺ How a Hash Map Works

  A hash map stores key-value pairs in an array of buckets. To insert or look up a key, it runs the key through a hash
  function, which produces an integer. That integer, reduced modulo the bucket count, picks the slot. Because the map
  jumps straight to a slot instead of scanning every entry, lookups take constant time on average.

  Two different keys can land in the same bucket, which is a collision. Implementations handle this with chaining (each
  bucket holds a small list) or open addressing (probe for the next free slot). When the table gets too full, it grows:
